newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy needs 20trln lire mini-budget for EMU - study.
newsitem.headline: Italy needs 20trln lire mini-budget for EMU - study.

text.p: Italy will need a 20 trillion lire mini-budget this year to ensure it keeps the ratio between its deficit and gross domestic product (GDP) to three percent, the economic research centre (CER) said in a survey.

Italy had a deficit/GDP ratio of around seven percent in 1996 and the three percent goal is one of the criteria laid out in the Maastricht Treaty for countries wishing to sign up to the planned single currency.
CER said the government could reduce the ratio to the three percent level this year with a deficit-cutting package of 14-15 trillion lire.
But it added that the ratio would widen again to four percent in 1998 unless 20 trillion lire of measures were introduced in the forthcoming mini-budget.
"It is not enough to hit the (three percent) target, you also have to maintain it," CER said.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi said earlier this week that the government had established the framework for a mini-budget and added that Italy was some six to 14 trillion lire short of reaching the three percent deficit target goal. ((-- Rome newsroom +396 6782501))
